teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A documented order conflict is useful only when the endpoint actually emits the declared status and body. Additional response metadata does not implement the outcome.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Declare known outcomes with responses={status: {"model": PublicModel, "description": ...}} alongside the main response_model and status_code.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: A responses declaration documents additional outcomes but does not make the handler produce them; return the actual matching response or raise the corresponding expected exception. Use response_description and outcome descriptions to explain what the successful and expected error bodies mean to clients. Compare generated response status entries and schemas with HTTP tests of the real success and expected error cases so documentation does not claim a body or status the endpoint does not emit.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Declare known outcomes using responses with public models and descriptions beside the main status and response_model. Exercise success and the expected error through HTTP and compare their status and bodies with generated entries. Use response_description and outcome descriptions to explain client meaning. If 409 is documented, the actual matching response or expected exception still needs to be produced by the operation.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: A responses entry documents an outcome; it does not make the handler return it.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the order endpoint's response declarations, generated status entries and schemas, and actual success and conflict HTTP results visible side by side so missing or misleading documentation can be located.

practice_anchor.objective: Document an existing order endpoint's successful response and expected 409 conflict using its supplied public models, then verify those declarations against HTTP results.
practice_anchor.success: The endpoint declares its main response_model and status_code, a meaningful response_description, and a 409 responses entry with the matching public model and description. Generated response entries and schemas agree with the supplied success and conflict HTTP tests.

live_code.required_skill: Add response metadata to a FastAPI path operation and compare documented statuses and body schemas with actual HTTP outcomes.
allowed_syntax: responses dictionaries with integer status keys and model and description entries
Existing return statements and HTTPException calls
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide one working order endpoint with a successful outcome and an expected 409 conflict, matching public models, and HTTP tests that exercise both paths. Leave response documentation incomplete without requiring changes to the supplied outcome implementation.
live_code.observable_success: Both HTTP cases retain their actual statuses and bodies. The generated response entries contain the corresponding public schemas and meaningful descriptions, with no documented outcome that contradicts either tested case.
